findings.text: Releases a virtual mapping descriptor by removing the tracked range for its recorded address from busy tracking, checking that the removed descriptor matches the supplied one, and then releasing the descriptor object.
Determines membership in the vmalloc address interval by stripping tag bits from the supplied pointer and comparing the untagged value against the lower and upper vmalloc bounds.

Determines whether an address belongs to modules or vmalloc space by accepting the module interval when that configuration is present and otherwise delegating to the vmalloc interval check, in both cases after tag normalization.

Candidate placement inside a free area is classified into five outcomes. A candidate starting before the area or ending beyond it is rejected as non fitting. Otherwise full coverage and left edge coincidence and right edge coincidence and strictly interior placement are distinguished. Source exposes these as NOTHING_FIT and FL_FIT_TYPE and LE_FIT_TYPE and RE_FIT_TYPE and NE_FIT_TYPE.

Carving an allocated extent from a free area follows the fit outcome. Full coverage removes the free descriptor from indexing and releases its object. Left edge coincidence advances the start bound of the free area by the allocated size. Right edge coincidence retreats the end bound to the allocated start. Interior placement splits the free area into a left remainder kept as a separate descriptor and a right remainder formed by advancing the original start past the allocated extent. Partial fits refresh augmented maxima and link any new remainder.

Free and busy areas are tracked by descriptors carrying a start bound and an end bound plus a tree node and a list linkage and a cached subtree maximum. Tree membership and list membership are updated together on link and unlink, with the tree node cleared after removal and the list linkage reinitialized. Augmented and non augmented variants select whether tree removal and insertion maintain maxima. Observed fields include va_start and va_end and rb_node and list and subtree_max_size and flags.

Per node state separates busy tracking and lazy tracking and sized pools and purge staging. Busy tracking holds a tree with its own lock. Lazy tracking holds a tree and queue with its own lock. Each size class holds a queue and length guarded by a pool lock. Purge staging uses a dedicated list and work item plus counters for purged descriptors and flags controlling repopulation. Observed members include busy and lazy and pool and pool_lock and purge_list and purge_work and nr_purged and skip_populate.

Small allocation blocks maintain counts of free slots and dirty slots with dirty interval bounds and a cpu association and a lock and linkage for free queue membership and purge staging and a back reference to the owning area. Queues are per cpu and hold free blocks and an address indexed structure for lookup. Observed members include free and dirty and dirty_min and dirty_max and cpu and lock and free_list and purge and va.

Removal from busy tracking occurs under the busy lock of the node derived from the area start, while insertion or merging into the global free structures occurs under the global free lock. Reclamation of lists into the global free tree also holds the global free lock across the whole merge sequence.

Lazy insertion holds the lazy lock of the selected node. Pool removal and addition and detach and reattach hold the pool lock of the owning node, with queue length updated as a single store. Lazy collection for purge detaches each non empty lazy tree and queue under its lazy lock before flushing address translations, and the whole purge holds the global purge mutex.

Scanning for fragmented blocks iterates per cpu free queues under read side protection, sampling free and dirty counts with single loads, then takes the block lock to attempt purge and takes the queue lock only when detaching a selected block from its free queue.

Preloading for interior splits allocates a spare descriptor outside the critical section when the current cpu cache is empty, then acquires the supplied lock and installs the spare with an atomic compare exchange, releasing it if another context already installed one.

Returning an area to free space merges with address adjacent siblings. A successor starting exactly at the returned end is expanded backward to absorb it, and a predecessor ending exactly at the resulting start is expanded forward to absorb it, with descriptor objects released for absorbed entries. When both sides merge, the successor entry is first detached before folding into the predecessor. Non adjacent areas are linked without merging.

The free tree caches in each descriptor the maximum free extent in its subtree as the maximum of its own extent and the cached maxima of its left and right children. Updates propagate from a changed node toward the root until the cached value stabilizes, and a debug check recomputes the same maximum for every free descriptor and reports mismatch.

Sized pools are selected by rounding the requested byte size up to page granularity. Indices below the configured page count limit map to the corresponding per node pool, while larger sizes have no pool and bypass pooling. Limit symbol is MAX_VA_SIZE_PAGES.

Node identity is translated between pointers and small integers by index arithmetic over a dense node array, with bounds checks that warn and fall back on out of range values. Stored flags carry an encoded form that reserves zero for absent and shifts valid identities by one byte, decoded symmetrically with validation against the live node count. Array and count are known as vmap_nodes and nr_vmap_nodes.

Freed areas enter lazy state under accounting of outstanding lazy pages and are queued on the originating node when its identity is valid, otherwise on the node derived from address. Crossing the lazy page threshold schedules a drain. Purging detaches lazy queues, flushes translations over the union range, then either returns descriptors to sized pools when repopulation is allowed or stages them for global reclaim, decrementing the lazy page count.

Pool maintenance detaches each size queue and either discards all entries on full decay or discards roughly one quarter on partial decay, merging discarded entries through a temporary tree before global reclaim and reattaching survivors with corrected length. Lazy purge work is spread over at most one worker per non empty node, limited by the number of outstanding lazy threshold multiples, with unassisted nodes purged synchronously and assisted nodes flushed after scheduling.

A block becomes eligible for purge only when the sum of free and dirty slots equals the block capacity and not all slots are dirty. Forced purges accept any such fragmented block, while opportunistic purges also require free slots below a threshold. Selected blocks are fenced against further allocation and reuse by clearing free count and marking fully dirty with widest dirty interval, detached from the free queue, staged for release, then removed from address indexing and busy tracking before releasing area and block objects.

Node scoped allocation applies only to the full vmalloc interval when more than one node exists, selecting a node by current cpu modulo node count. It attempts pool removal requiring exact size match and interval containment and alignment, moving a misaligned head entry to the tail instead of using it, and reports the pool address on success.

Interior splits require an extra descriptor normally supplied by per cpu preload. If the current cpu cache is empty, a non sleeping allocation is attempted and failure is reported as out of memory to trigger higher level purge and retry, rather than proceeding with a corrupted split.

Requests outside the free area or with an unrecognized fit outcome are rejected as invalid without modifying indexing. Neighbor lookup on an empty tree yields no sibling and merging degrades to plain insertion, handling absence of free space explicitly.

Unlinking a descriptor already detached from the tree triggers a warning and leaves state unchanged. Pool removal validates exact size and interval containment and warns once on mismatch without consuming the entry. Encoded and decoded node identities outside the live range warn and fall back to neutral values.
The vmalloc interval lower and upper limits define validity for address predicates and for node scoped allocation eligibility. Relevant limits are known as VMALLOC_START and VMALLOC_END.
Page size and page shift define conversion between byte extents and page counts for pool indexing and lazy accounting and purge thresholds. Relevant symbols include PAGE_SIZE and PAGE_SHIFT.
A byte width shift separates stored flag payload from encoded node identity, reserving one value for absent identity. Width symbol is BITS_PER_BYTE.

Block capacity in slots and block byte size and purge free threshold govern eligibility for fragmented block reclamation and address to block sharding. Relevant symbols include VMAP_BBMAP_BITS and VMAP_BLOCK_SIZE and VMAP_PURGE_THRESHOLD.

Block lookup shards addresses across per cpu structures by dividing by block size modulo cpu count, advancing to the next possible cpu when the computed slot is impossible, and derives a block index by subtracting the aligned vmalloc base before dividing by block size.

Purge of node lazy areas optionally releases sanitizer state for entries inside vmalloc or module ranges with periodic rescheduling, followed by a range wide release associated with translation flush.
